acceptance_condition: Stated and proved theorems: an explicit upper bound N(H) <= f(H) with constants, the proof of the per-edge growth factor and branching bounds it rests on, and a rigorous two-sided depth-log H relation; any sharper-but-unproved improvement must be labeled as conjecture with supporting reasoning kept separate from the proved bound.
rationale: D4 (upper side) and D6 (depth vs log H) share the same engine - the multiplicative growth of the maximum along tree edges - so coupling them avoids duplicate lemma work and yields the strongest combined statement.
text: From first principles, prove the strongest rigorous upper bound attainable for N(H), the number of sorted solutions with maximum coordinate at most H, and analyze rigorously how mutation depth (distance from the root (1,1,1,1), well-defined once the tree structure holds) relates to log H. Expected components, to be proved or improved: (i) every child of a non-root vertex has maximum at least 3 times the parent's maximum (since mutating at any coordinate below the maximum d gives a new value >= (4ab-1)d with ab >= 1), hence depth(v) <= log_3(max(v)) and max(v) >= 3^{depth(v)}; (ii) every non-root vertex has at most 3 children and the root has exactly 1, giving a crude N(H) = O(H); (iii) sharpen the O(H) bound as far as rigorously possible (e.g., by analyzing coincidences between children, forced sorting effects, or refined growth factors larger than 3 on most branches), and give a two-sided relation between depth and log H along extremal branches (fastest- and slowest-growing chains). No growth law may be assumed; every bound must come with explicit constants and complete proofs.
